# AV Gen over MCP

<!-- Generated by `avgen --describe all` from src/api/mcp_shaper.cpp and the tool catalogue (ADR-2162). Do not edit by hand: run tools/gen_api.sh. -->

`avgen mcp` serves the engine's tools to a Model Context Protocol client on stdin and stdout, protocol revision **2025-11-25**. It is `avgen serve` (see [protocol.md](protocol.md)) with a different result shaper: the same loop, the same session, the same `Session::call`, the same 98 tools ([tools.md](tools.md)). Nothing here is a second implementation of a tool, so a tool behaves the same through Studio, `avgen call`, `avgen serve` and `avgen mcp`.

## Client configuration

Most MCP clients take a `mcpServers` block. Give the session a root: the folder it may read and write (projects, imported assets, renders). Without one, every file tool is refused `PERMISSION_DENIED`.

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "avgen": {
      "command": "/path/to/avgen",
      "args": ["mcp", "--root", "/path/to/work"]
    }
  }
}
```

The flags are `avgen serve`'s: `--root <dir>` (read and write), `--read-root <dir>`, `--write-root <dir>` (each repeatable) and `--allow-subprocess`. The log is on stderr. The process opens no socket and no window; a GPU device is made only when the first render job starts, under the machine's GPU lock.

## Protocol revision

The server speaks `2025-11-25` and only that, the newest revision that opens with `initialize`. `initialize` always answers it; a client that cannot speak it disconnects. Revision 2026-07-28 replaced the handshake with per-request `_meta` and `server/discover`; a client that speaks both probes `server/discover`, receives `-32601` (method not found) and falls back to `initialize`. The revision is one constant, `api::kMcpProtocolRevision`, and the shape tests name it.

## Methods and notifications

| Method | Kind | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `initialize` | request | Must be the first request. Takes `{protocolVersion, capabilities, clientInfo}`; answers `{protocolVersion, capabilities: {tools: {listChanged: false}, logging: {}}, serverInfo, instructions, _meta}`. `protocolVersion` is always the pinned revision: the client's when it asked for that one, else the pinned one, for the client to accept or disconnect. `_meta["avgen/server"]` is what `avgen serve`'s `initialize` answers (the API level, the versions, the session and its permissions). A second `initialize` is refused. |
| `notifications/initialized` | notification | The client is ready. Requests sent before it are still answered (the server is lenient), and the server sends no notification it was not asked for before it. |
| `ping` | request | Answers `{}`. Allowed at any time, also before `initialize`. |
| `tools/list` | request | Every tool, in one page (no `nextCursor`; a `cursor` is refused `-32602`). Each is the catalogue entry shaped as an MCP Tool: `name` is its `mcpName`, `annotations` carry `readOnlyHint`, `destructiveHint`, `idempotentHint` and `openWorldHint: false`, and `_meta` names the canonical tool and its availability in this session. |
| `tools/call` | request | Takes `{name, arguments?, _meta?}`. `name` is looked up in the name table (an unknown one is `-32602`), then the tool runs through `Session::call`, as for every client. Answers `CallToolResult {content, structuredContent, isError}`. `_meta` may carry `progressToken`, `avgen/transaction` (join the open explicit transaction), `avgen/irreversible` (`true`, `"accept"` or `"refuse"`) and `avgen/dryRun`. |
| `logging/setLevel` | request | Takes `{level}` (`debug`, `info`, `notice`, `warning`, `error`, `critical`, `alert`, `emergency`): which of the engine's log lines reach the client as `notifications/message`. The default is `warning`. |
| `notifications/cancelled` | notification | Accepted and ignored: a call runs to its end (the server does not support cancellation; `job.cancel` stops a render job). |
| `notifications/progress` | server notification | `{progressToken, progress, total: 1, message}`, sent only while the `tools/call` that supplied `_meta.progressToken` runs: the tool's own progress, and for `job.wait` the waited job's state and phase (waiting for the GPU lock, compiling pipelines, playing history, rendering). `progress` only increases; a repeat of the last message with no more progress is not sent. |
| `notifications/message` | server notification | `{level, logger: "avgen", data}`: an engine log line at or above the level `logging/setLevel` chose. |

Any other method is `-32601`. A batch (a JSON array) is `-32600`: this revision has no batches. A request before `initialize` (except `ping`) is `-32600`. End of input closes the session: an open explicit transaction is rolled back, and nothing is saved.

## Results

`tools/call` answers a `CallToolResult`:

- `structuredContent` is the envelope every client receives (`docs/api/protocol.md`): `success`, `result`, `summary`, `changes`, `warnings`, `transaction`, `job`, and `error {code, message, recovery, details?}` on failure. It is the same JSON `avgen serve` answers for the same call.
- `isError` is `!success`. A tool failure, including invalid arguments and a refused permission, is a result with `isError: true`, so the model can read the error and retry.
- `content[0]` is a text block: the summary, a newline, and the envelope as compact JSON, for clients that do not read `structuredContent`.
- **Files are paths.** A capture or render lists its outputs as absolute paths in the job record (`job_wait`'s `result.outputs[].path`, with `sha256` and the frame hashes). No image is inlined.
- Each tool's `outputSchema` describes the envelope, with the tool's own output schema under `result` (or `{}` for a tool that has none yet).

An **unknown tool name** is a protocol error, as MCP has it: `-32602` with `data {name, recovery}`. `avgen serve` answers the same mistake with a tool result (`NOT_FOUND`); that is the one place the two differ.

## Transactions

MCP has no field for them, so they ride in `tools/call`'s `_meta`: `{"avgen/transaction": "txn-1"}` joins the explicit transaction `transaction_begin` opened, and `{"avgen/irreversible": true}` accepts a call a rollback cannot undo. While one is open, a mutating call that does not name it is refused `FAILED_PRECONDITION` ([transactions.md](transactions.md)). A client that cannot set `_meta` should not open an explicit transaction: every call outside one runs in an implicit transaction of its own, rolled back if it fails.

## The name table

MCP clients accept tool names matching `^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{1,64}$`; AV Gen's are `domain.verb`. Each tool's `mcpName` is generated into the catalogue, and `tools/call` maps it back through this table, never by reversing the string.
